author: Danielle Smith
title: Federal plan for AI data centers in PA drops key environmental protections - NewsBreak
text: Conservation groups warn the Trump administration’s long-term plan for artificial intelligence will have long-term environmental impacts in Pennsylvania and elsewhere.The plan calls for the removal of environmental and land-use rules considered prohibitive to the construction of AI data centers.Ben Murray, senior researcher for the advocacy group Food and Water Watch, said fossil fuel plants are already being reopened to help power their high energy demand."We just need to be aware that anything that prolongs our reliance on fossil fuel is going to increase the problems that we’re seeing from the climate crisis," Murray explained.In Pennsylvania, the former Homer City coal plant will be redeveloped into a 4.5-gigawatt gas facility, with construction starting this year and power generation expected by 2027.Murray argued technological advancements should not come at the expense of the planet or increase household energy prices. The Trump administration believes environmental and permitting regulations will only slow America’s dominance in the AI field.Computer servers driving AI require far more energy than standard applications. A ChatGPT query, for example, can use up to 10 times as much electricity to process as a typical Google search. Murray pointed out the drive for more data centers is already leading Big Tech companies to backtrack on their climate goals."These companies can seem as if they’re decreasing their emissions and meeting net-zero goals but in reality emissions are amping up faster than ever for these companies," Murray emphasized.A report last year found emissions from data centers owned by Apple, Google, Meta and Microsoft were more than seven times higher than officially reported. Murray stressed it is possible to power AI services with renewable energy sources but it requires political will.
